Development only: quarantined assets, unreviewed content, no source/content/reuse approval. Worlds are produced by the shared generator (@ottie/scenario-core createDevelopmentGenerator) from the pinned template, seed, source profile and registry hash; nothing here is a hand-authored world.
title: Give Way at a T junction
summary: A minor access road joins an east-west major road. The ego car approaches northbound behind the RMS2 marking D double broken line with a TFM1 GIVE WAY face on the left verge. One world has a lorry approaching on the major road from the ego's left while the ego turns right; the other has the major road clear while the ego turns left.

worlds.label: Right turn onto the major road; lorry approaching from the left
notes: majorRoadVehicle.approach=west places the lorry eastbound on major.with.0, i.e. approaching from the ego's LEFT. The right turn (minor.with.0.right) conflicts with major.with.0.straight, so ev.priority-relationship names a real conflict.

Selected deliberately instead of a left turn with a vehicle from the far side: those configurations are the known C2 finding (question_evidence.priority_evidence_without_conflict) and are not authored here.

worlds.label: Left turn onto the major road; no major-road traffic in view
notes: majorRoadVehicle.approach=none: the template emits no major-road actor and no priority evidence. majorRoadVehicle.category is pinned only so the request is fully explicit; the layout does not use it here.
Used for the 'stop only if necessary' half of the Give Way meaning: with the major road clear the learner slows and proceeds without a compulsory stop.

unknowns: The generated world keeps the F0 schematic post (2.1 m mount, dimensionsStatus schematic_unsourced). A2 lists SUP6/SUP5/SUP15 candidates with a printed 2400 mm sign-bottom clearance on those sheets only and SUP7 with no installation height; choosing one is an I1/C2 layout change, not a T1 content choice, and 2400 mm is not a universal mounting rule.

comparisons.label: Same junction with a STOP control instead
comparisons.generationNote: A STOP control at this junction is not a configuration of sg.t-junction.give-way@1, and sg.t-junction.stop@1 is a different layout. The delta is declarative; applying it to the base world is a comparison-applier responsibility (I1/renderer), not a T1 regeneration.

comparisons.label: Same clear junction with a STOP control instead
Same junction with a bus instead of the lorry

exclusions: Pedestrian crossings (zebra, signalised, school) are not placed: no starter marking or sign for them has been separately sourced.
Lane separators B/C, edge/yellow lines, box markings and centre paint variants are outside the starter paint scope (A1 README); the layout places only the RMS2 D control line.
No traffic lights: the junction is unsignalised and the template emits no signal head or controller.

sourceRefs.quote: Slow down. Stop if necessary. Give way to traffic on major road
Parallel broken white lines indicate that traffic approaching these lines must give way to traffic on a major road.

sourceRefs.section: §81 The 'Give Way' Rule At Road Junctions
sourceRefs.quote: When approaching a junction with a major road, slow down gradually and give way to traffic on the major road.

unresolved: The handbook does not define 'major road' formally; the starter term major-road is glossary-only (A3 rule give-way-at-double-broken-line unresolved note, preserved).
Whether a Give Way sign is always accompanied by marking D is not stated by TP or SDRE; this package pairs them because the C2 layout does, not because a source requires it.
Sign mounting height, post and the 1 m line setback in the generated world are schematic teaching choices recorded in the world's provenance notes, not source values.
